title: Teach the Cleaner Without Peeking
key_insight: Any cleaning rule that learns from values—such as a typical replacement number—must learn from training rows only.
body:
## The Cleaner Peeks at the Test Answers

A blank test value is filled using the average from the entire table. That average contains information from the held-out rows, so the training process has quietly peeked ahead.

First split the data. Then let each cleaner learn only from training rows: an imputer learns replacement values, an encoder learns categories, and a scaler learns ranges.

Save those learned rules and apply them unchanged to later rows. A pipeline keeps the order together and prevents the cleaner and model from seeing different versions of the data.
common_mistakes: Filling blanks or scaling columns before the train/test split.
Using zero for every missing value without asking what zero means in that column.
Encoding categories differently in training and production.
Removing unusual values merely because they are rare.
mini_exercise: Split a tiny table first, find the training median for one numeric column, and use that same median to fill blanks on both sides.
real_world_usage: Machine-learning pipelines fit imputers, encoders, and scalers with training data, then store them beside the model so new requests receive identical preparation.
explain_back_prompt: Why can a data cleaner leak test information, and how does fitting the cleaner after the split prevent it?

build_task.title: Clean a small customer table
build_task.context: Turn a deliberately messy table into consistent model-ready rows without hiding what changed.
steps: Create a pandas table with a missing age, a repeated row, and two spellings of the same city.
Remove only the true duplicate and make the city spellings consistent.
Split the rows, learn the training median age, and fill missing ages with that saved value.
Print the cleaned table and a short count of each repair.
build_task.expected_output: A table with no accidental duplicate, one spelling per city, and no missing age, plus counts showing each repair.
build_task.hint: Split before learning the median; the test rows must not help choose it.
